title: Wire production child accounting + enforce the C1 job-object containment gate in the start launch path
objective: QUALIFYING EVIDENCE (supervisor-freeze section 2/3): M0-T052 G5 security review (project-control/reports/M0-T052-g5-security.md) SEC-MAJOR - demonstrated security risk: (a) record_launched_child (recovery.py:181) has NO production caller, so recover_boot's surviving-child fail-closed is inert in production (the runner spawns via subprocess.Popen + container.adopt at claude_runner.py:965-971 without journaling the pid); (b) kill-on-close containment is platform-conditional (Job Object only) and cmd_start has no fail-closed containment gate, so on non-Job-Object hosts a stranded-START_CLAUDE resume (M0-T052) could double-launch over an orphaned worker. SCOPE (smallest durable set, G5 C1+C2 verbatim): (1) call record_launched_child at worker spawn and clear_child_record on verified clean exit, in the production launch path, so a surviving recorded child forces UNSAFE_OR_DRIFTED refusal on resume; (2) enforce the C1 activation pin fail-closed IN THE START LAUNCH PATH: refuse supervised dispatch when the host's default containment is not the Job Object (doctor-parity check at cmd_start/loop construction), with an explicit refusal reason; (3) correct nothing else - no redesign (D-010-R240 pattern). REQUIRED TESTS: surviving-recorded-child refusal now exercised through the PRODUCTION recording path (spawn->record->kill supervisor->resume refuses); clean-exit clears the record and the subsequent resume proceeds; non-job-object containment refuses supervised dispatch fail-closed with the recorded reason; full supervisor suite re-establishes the M0-T052 baseline (1402 passed/2 skipped) plus the new tests, 0 failures.
business_reason: M0-T052 G5 required corrections C1 (host containment precondition, launch-path enforcement) and C2 (child-accounting wiring) - BLOCKING for continued supervised-auto operation beyond the verified Job-Object host; closes the double-launch residual so protection does not rest on kill-on-close alone.
forbidden_paths: tools/agent_supervisor/** (modules not named in allowed_paths: smallest durable set only; wider need = STOP-and-report)
services/**, apps/**, packages/** (M2-T015 scope stays untouched)

G5 SECURITY REVIEW (independent security-reviewer, read-only): VERDICT PASS, analysis COMPLETE, no BLOCKING finding. It REPRODUCED the producer's headline exactly by running the suite itself: 1493 passed / 2 skipped. Q1 answered YES - the double-launch hole closes on the real production path; it traced cli.py:2269 (the only non-test ClaudeRunner, now passing journal=journal) -> Popen -> container.adopt -> record BEFORE the first write -> settle gated on poll(), and confirmed the mechanism is genuinely non-inert because loop.py transitions START_CLAUDE->CLAUDE_RUNNING only AFTER run_unit returns while START_CLAUDE is in CYCLE_ENTRY_STATES, so a mid-unit kill really does leave a legal re-entry that would have dispatched a second worker. It found NO path where a live child exists unrecorded and NO path where a record is cleared while the child lives, except finding 4's compound. It also CORRECTED the producer's framing of R1: R1 does not stand alone, because the gate admits only job_object hosts where KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE + non-inheritable handle means the kernel kills the child - R1 is reachable only via R4. Also caught a transcription slip (producer said 15 deselected; real number 16) while confirming the baseline 1481 and delta +12 are correct. It re-verified the single-call-site claim itself and went further than the producer by checking the adjacent knob: RunnerConfig.use_job_object defaults True and is set from NO cli arg or config anywhere, so there is no config-side route to pass the gate then spawn uncontained. Drove all four host shapes live. Its sandbox hook blocked programmatic test-runner invocation so it could NOT re-run the mutation matrix - it said so plainly and verified the guards from the other side by driving production code in memory instead (settle retains on poll()=None and clears on poll()=0; unwritable journal refuses with child_record_unwritable, calls terminate_all+close, closes all three pipes, chains the OSError cause). CORRECTION TO A FALSE CLAIM I RECORDED: I wrote 'doctor parity is structural' in this task's progress log and in the PR #218 body. That is HALF TRUE and must not stand unqualified. The gate and doctor share default_containment_kind(), so the reported KIND cannot diverge - but the VERDICTS do: _check_containment_default() (cli.py:1102-1129) returns ok=True on POSIX when kind is process_group (line 1124 sets expected per-OS) and ok=True on a Windows host that refuses a Job Object (1119-1123). So on Linux doctor prints 'containment_default: ok' while the gate REFUSES. The direction is safe (the gate is stricter) so it is not a defect, but the 2026-08-08 pin's criterion (1) is worded 'doctor reports containment_default: ok, job_object', and an operator checking only the ok flag on a non-Windows host would wrongly believe criterion (1) was met. Correct wording is 'same containment SOURCE', not 'doctor parity'. OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE FOR MERGE, not previously surfaced: the gate is unconditional on mode, so 'start' now HARD-REFUSES on every POSIX host including Render, and including shadow mode (shadow does spawn a real worker). The supervisor is now Windows-job-object-only. That matches the pin's 'any run that spawns a live worker' and breaks nothing today, but it is a real deployment narrowing the owner should know about. CONVERGENCE: its MINOR finding 1 (clear_child_record whole-key wipe) independently matches G5's P2, and it independently raised the uncontained doctor --live preflight probe that G5 raised as its finding 6 - two reviewers, no communication, same two items. On R4 it judges deferral DEFENSIBLE and NOT false assurance, agreeing with G5, because the payload and refusal text say 'default' throughout and never claim an achieved guarantee, and enforcing criterion (2) means stopping the loop mid-run, which supervisor-freeze section 1 forbids in this packet. Its extra MINOR items: killing a live worker for an unjournalable pid writes NOTHING to the audit log though the runner holds self.audit; the unwritable-record test asserts only the error code so deleting terminate_all() keeps the suite green (coverage gap, behaviour verified present); and the start payload key 'containment' reads as achieved containment but is the host precondition.
